GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: The nine defects come from the 2026-11-02 smart review of the 2.9.x-next train (report: ~/Documents/mark-review-2.9.x-next-2026-11-02.md, base v2.8.2 3b6d49e4, head f3d88851) and were independently re-verified by direct code read in the authoring session before the spec was written: the four rollback blockers (m068_rollback.rs 639-644, 672, 1010, 1028-1029), the instance-lock race (872-889), the relaunch-error path (657-659) and the worker.mjs index field all confirmed as described. The review's own numbers: 16 rollback tests and 18 gateway tests pass today, so none of these failures is covered by an existing test — every fix here ships with its regression test. One combined change (not three) because the rollback defects share one file and one verification surface, the gateway defects share another, and the train window before freeze is one; the owner chose this scope explicitly (2026-11-02, translated from Russian: "Одна спека: откат + шлюз" — one spec: rollback + gateway; then "Approve + добавить находки 5-6", adding the instance-lock race and the false-success CLI outcome to the original 4+3 scope). The LINKS hygiene rides along because both files are open anyway and the stale runtime.xml references misroute future readers.

Alternatives.Alternative: Three separate changes (rollback blockers / rollback findings 5-6 / gateway wire format): rejected — same files, same test suites, one train window; the owner explicitly picked one spec.

Fold the gateway fixes into the draft C-STATS-READOUT change: rejected — that draft is a readout feature building on the same SQL this change repairs; fixes are its prerequisite and must land first, so the readout rebases instead of carrying them.

Defer everything to 2.9.1: rejected by the owner — rollback integrity defects (a restore that can wipe settings before verification or leave macOS without an application) ship in this train only if fixed before freeze.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Exact MARK_ROLLBACK outcome token for a completed restore whose relaunch failed (distinct event vs restored-with-detail) — fixed at implementation inside T-006's acceptance criteria; either form satisfies R-5's "0 restored and relaunched" truthfulness as long as plain success is never reported.

Exact swap-aside mechanism (sibling temp name scheme) inside T-001 — any scheme that never deletes the departed bundle before the replacement rename confirms and restores it on failure satisfies the criterion.

Where snapshot strictness lives: the default is m068 pre-parsing the snapshot as a valid object before any mutation; the alternative — m005's replace_from_snapshot itself becoming strict — is recorded but not silently available: it requires a plan amendment first (m005_prefs.rs into ObservedWriteScope, M-005 into GraphAnchors and AffectedAreas), so an implementer cannot drift out of scope on it.

The mark-site exit-table row for restored_norelaunch is in scope as plan task T-012 (same wave as the code — the archived R-7 precedent; the sibling mark-site repository (../mark-site), deploy separate), not a follow-up; the owed owner-side step that remains is the live smoke: one real query.mjs --live run plus one gateway check through the deployed worker after the owner's next deploy, since no credential exists in CI.

Three pre-existing defects beyond the nine, found by review-gate rounds 1-2 and confirmed by code read or on-machine experiment, deferred together as one tracked rollback-integrity follow-up: the GUI's lockless start when the CLI already holds the instance lock (main.rs:717-720 has no else branch; mt_rollback_restore takes no lock of its own); the delegation ack written before the dialog emit (m068_rollback.rs:786-802, making R-5's exit-6 broken-dialog path unreachable, with a predictable unix-seconds nonce at :873 — same-user deception only, within the accepted R-3 bound); and R-3's Windows pending-window serialization ("a staging-area lock or marker"), never implemented — the M-068 graph Summary's "the staging lock serialize everything" claim is false today, and T-010 removes the false claim while the requirement itself stays with this follow-up.

The localization follow-up (review finding 14) also owns the new user-visible English strings this change produces or rewords (T-001/T-002 error texts, T-006 guidance) and the absent user surface for a post-swap preferences-write skip in the GUI (today a stderr marker only — the no-renderer-changes constraint accepts that bound); the mark-site row is not part of this follow-up — it ships as plan task T-012 in the same wave.

Scenarios.Scenario: macOS: the staged-bundle rename fails after the current bundle moved aside — the swap routine renames the departed bundle back to the running path and returns an error; the user's application is exactly as before, the error names the failure.

The preferences snapshot file is corrupt JSON — the GUI restore aborts before any mutation (no empty-map wipe through m005's load_from fallback), the rollback set stays, a retry after fixing the file works.
Windows: the feed fetch fails or the minisignature does not verify after the user confirmed — the command returns its verification error with preferences and skippedUpdateVersion byte-unchanged.
Boot reconciliation meets an invalid staging manifest or a promotion rename failure — the existing live set survives untouched; the failed staging never becomes live.
A second CLI --rollback runs while the first holds the instance lock — the second takes the delegate-or-decline path and performs no restore work, exactly as R-5 specifies.
The restore swap succeeds but relaunch fails — the machine-readable outcome says so distinctly and the terminal prints how to start the restored app; nothing reports plain success.
query.mjs --live against a real Analytics Engine response — rows arrive in data with an index1 column and both tables print; a dry run still prints the inlined fixtures.

Old datapoints written before this fix, if any exist (unproven — the invalid write may have failed silently), coexist with new ones — the live query neither crashes nor invents a label; today's renderer drops unnamed events from both tables, so the breakdown reads as post-fix-only, and the owner-side live smoke settles the actual dataset.

C-1.Name: Half-swap impossibility
C-1.Situation: Any failure between moving the current bundle aside and the staged bundle arriving at the running path.
C-1.Expected: The departed bundle returns to the running path before the error surfaces; Trash receives a bundle only after its replacement confirmed; a hard crash between the two renames leaves the path empty with the bundle recoverable at the deterministic aside name — the guarantee is recoverability at a known path (the documented manual window), never an unreachable empty state.

C-2.Name: Verification-before-mutation everywhere
C-2.Situation: Digest mismatch, corrupt snapshot, feed failure, signature failure — at any point before the system is touched.
C-2.Expected: Every such failure returns with preferences, skip key and bundle byte-identical to pre-run state; the accepted soft-failure states are named: a logged preferences write error on macOS after a confirmed swap (per R-3), and on Windows a spawn failure after the last-write prefs (set intact, retry idempotent, per R-3's pending semantics).

C-3.Name: Promotion never destroys the escape hatch
C-3.Situation: reconcile_at_boot with invalid staging, or a filesystem error mid-promotion.
C-3.Expected: The previous live set survives both; an invalid manifest never becomes live; the only deletion happens after the replacement confirmed.

C-4.Name: Lock lifetime
C-4.Situation: Concurrent CLI invocations, or a GUI instance starting while a headless restore runs.
C-4.Expected: The first successful lock acquisition is held for the process lifetime — no probe-then-reacquire window; a losing CLI delegates or declines without touching anything (a GUI starter is lockless today — main.rs:717-720 — that window belongs to the deferred T-013 follow-up, not to this change's guarantees).

C-5.Name: Gateway stays best-effort and dumb
C-5.Situation: The wire-shape fix and any binding behavior change.
C-5.Expected: /feed and /pkg behavior is byte-identical; the write happens inside waitUntil with failures swallowed; the fix changes only the datapoint's field name, never response semantics.

C-6.Name: Pre-fix datapoints
C-6.Situation: Whatever the already-deployed worker's invalid index field actually wrote — unproven without live credentials (the writes may have failed silently, in which case no pre-fix rows or dataset exist at all).
C-6.Expected: No claim either way: if pre-fix rows exist, today's renderer drops unnamed events silently (byDay filters zero-sum named cells at query.mjs:68; fromBreakdown counts only event=check at :70), so the from-breakdown reads as post-fix-only; no migration is attempted (three-month retention ages anything out); the owner-side live smoke — recorded below as an owed step — settles what is actually in the dataset.

C-7.Name: C-STATS-READOUT coexistence
C-7.Situation: The readout draft edits the same three gateway files after this change.
C-7.Expected: This change lands first and the readout rebases; the readout's /stats route inherits a repaired SQL and wire shape instead of building on broken ones.

C-8.Name: Train discipline
C-8.Situation: The fixes are ready while 2.9.x-next is still Collecting.
C-8.Expected: Admission is a separate chore(train) commit after the PR is green with its testing protocol; no version bump, tag or release follows from this change; freeze/seal boundaries are untouched.

C-9.Name: App Store builds
C-9.Expected: Nothing: the rollback surface is feature-gated away in store builds and the gateway is desktop-updater-only; store builds neither see nor execute any of this code.
